spec.description: The ancestry of the United States by census tract, after The New York Times' map of July 2026: one dot per 250 people, the leading group of each tract, the share of any of 158 groups and H3 hexagons, from the American Community Survey 2024.

options.content:
# The ancestry mosaic of the United States

A replica, with Kepler.gl in Grafana, of the ancestry map *The New York Times* published in July 2026. The NYT does not publish its derived dataset, but it does state its source, and that source is open: the **American Community Survey 2024 (5-year)** from the U.S. Census Bureau, a work of the federal government and therefore in the public domain. Pacha builds its files once per instance, straight from www2.census.gov and with no API key (`datasets/ancestry/build.sh`).

**158 groups · 85,044 census tracts · 338 million people.** Tables
[B04006](https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/groups/B04006.html) (reported ancestry),
[B03001](https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/groups/B03001.html) (detailed Hispanic origin) and
[B02015](https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/groups/B02015.html) (detailed Asian groups);
geometry from the TIGER 2024 *cartographic boundary files*.

**How to read it.** Ancestry in the ACS is self-reported and multiple-response, and the three tables do not share a universe, so per-tract totals are renormalised where they overlap; the remainder shows up as *not reported*. The Census is forbidden by law from asking about religion, so groups defined by it do not exist in these data. And only seven groups get a colour of their own: a dot map is an all-against-all colour problem, and seven is the most that keeps the pairs distinguishable under colour blindness. The rest fall into *Other groups* — the bar chart and the table show what is inside, and the choropleth reaches all 158 one at a time.

*Pan and zoom on the main map: the other panels follow its viewport.*

spec.rawSql:
-- Un punto por cada 250 habitantes, coloreado por su grupo.
-- Dos recortes, no uno. El primero es el encuadre del mapa: kepler escribe
-- west/south/east/north y DuckDB poda por estadísticas de row-group, porque el
-- Parquet está ordenado espacialmente (celda H3 res 3).
-- El segundo es de densidad. A escala metropolitana entran los cuatro buckets y
-- Chicago rinde ~28.000 puntos; a escala nacional serían 1,35 millones y 86 MB,
-- así que se queda un bucket de cada cuatro. Los buckets recorren la secuencia
-- de puntos de cada tract, que está ordenada por grupo, de modo que cualquier
-- subconjunto conserva las proporciones (verificado: ±0,5 puntos).
SELECT latitude, longitude, ancestry, color_group, state
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/dots.parquet')
WHERE longitude BETWEEN ${west:raw} AND ${east:raw}
  AND latitude  BETWEEN ${south:raw} AND ${north:raw}
  AND bucket < CASE
        WHEN (${east:raw} - (${west:raw})) * (${north:raw} - (${south:raw})) > 100 THEN 1
        WHEN (${east:raw} - (${west:raw})) * (${north:raw} - (${south:raw})) > 5   THEN 2
        ELSE 4 END

spec.description: Dot density, the technique that reproduces the effect of the NYT map: kepler does not blend colours, but the overlap of neighbouring dots reads as a blend. This panel sends its viewport to the rest of the dashboard through viewportVariables.
spec.title: The mosaic · one dot = 250 people

spec.rawSql:
-- Polígonos de census tract coloreados por su ascendencia mayoritaria.
-- El CAST a VARCHAR no es decorativo: ST_AsGeoJSON devuelve el tipo JSON de
-- DuckDB y el driver Go del datasource no puede escanearlo a string. kepler
-- tampoco renderiza WKB, así que la geometría tiene que llegar como GeoJSON.
SELECT t.geoid, t.name, t.county, t.state, t.total_pop,
       t.top1_ancestry, t.top1_color_group, round(100 * t.top1_pct, 1) AS top1_porcentaje,
       t.top2_ancestry, t.top3_ancestry,
       CAST(ST_AsGeoJSON(g.geometry) AS VARCHAR) AS geojson
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts-geom.parquet') g
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts.parquet') t USING (geoid)
WHERE g.maxx > ${west:raw} AND g.minx < ${east:raw} AND g.maxy > ${south:raw} AND g.miny < ${north:raw}
ORDER BY t.total_pop DESC
LIMIT 6000

spec.description: Polygons served as GeoJSON out of GeoParquet. The clip uses the four bounding-box columns rather than ST_Intersects: a BETWEEN over DOUBLE is pruned by Parquet's row-group statistics, whereas the intersection would force all 85k geometries to be decoded.
spec.title: Majority ancestry by census tract

spec.rawSql:
-- Un solo grupo, escala secuencial. Cubre los 158 grupos del fixture,
-- no solo los siete que tienen color propio en el mosaico.
SELECT t.geoid, t.name, t.county, t.state, a.ancestry, a.estimate AS personas,
       round(100 * a.pct, 2) AS pct,
       CAST(ST_AsGeoJSON(g.geometry) AS VARCHAR) AS geojson
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tract-ancestry.parquet') a
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts-geom.parquet') g USING (geoid)
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts.parquet') t USING (geoid)
WHERE a.ancestry = '${grupo:raw}' AND g.maxx > ${west:raw} AND g.minx < ${east:raw} AND g.maxy > ${south:raw} AND g.miny < ${north:raw}
ORDER BY t.total_pop DESC
LIMIT 6000

spec.description: A single-hue sequential scale over the percentage of the group chosen in the variable. It covers all 158 groups, including those the mosaic folds into "Other groups". Same 6,000-tract ceiling as the panel on the left.
spec.title: Choropleth · $grupo

spec.rawSql:
-- Agregado a 25k celdas, así que se carga entero: este panel no filtra por
-- encuadre. El índice H3 viene precalculado en el Parquet porque el datasource
-- DuckDB sólo carga la extensión spatial, y h3 es una extensión community.
SELECT h3, count, dominant_ancestry, dominant_color_group
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/h3.parquet')

spec.description: Height by population, colour by dominant group. The only map that does not filter by viewport: these are 25,197 aggregated cells and they fit whole.
spec.title: H3 hexagons · population and dominant group

spec.rawSql:
-- A diferencia de los mapas, los paneles que agregan sí recortan en SQL. Aquí se
-- usan los cuatro buckets siempre: agregar 1,35 millones de filas en DuckDB es
-- barato, y devuelve quince.
SELECT d.ancestry AS "Grupo", count(*) * 250 AS "Personas (aprox.)"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/dots.parquet') d
WHERE d.longitude BETWEEN ${west:raw} AND ${east:raw}
  AND d.latitude  BETWEEN ${south:raw} AND ${north:raw}
  AND d.ancestry <> 'Sin ascendencia reportada'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 15

spec.description: What is inside "Other groups". It aggregates in SQL, unlike the maps.
spec.title: The 15 largest groups in the viewport

spec.rawSql:
SELECT t.name AS "Tract", t.county AS "Condado", t.state_abbr AS "Est.",
       t.total_pop AS "Población",
       t.top1_ancestry AS "1º", round(100 * t.top1_pct, 1) AS "1º %",
       t.top2_ancestry AS "2º", round(100 * t.top2_pct, 1) AS "2º %",
       t.top3_ancestry AS "3º", round(100 * t.top3_pct, 1) AS "3º %"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts.parquet') t
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts-geom.parquet') g USING (geoid)
WHERE g.maxx > ${west:raw} AND g.minx < ${east:raw} AND g.maxy > ${south:raw} AND g.miny < ${north:raw}
ORDER BY t.total_pop DESC LIMIT 500

spec.description: The top three groups of each tract, which is what a map's colour cannot show at once.
spec.title: Census tracts in the viewport

spec.rawSql:
-- El CAST importa. sum() sobre un BIGINT devuelve HUGEINT en DuckDB, y el
-- driver Go del datasource entrega HUGEINT como string: el panel stat recibe
-- entonces un campo de texto, no puede reducirlo y se queda en blanco. Es el
-- mismo tipo de tropiezo que el CAST de ST_AsGeoJSON en los paneles de mapa.
SELECT sum(t.total_pop)::BIGINT AS "Población en el encuadre",
       count(*) AS "Census tracts",
       count(DISTINCT t.top1_ancestry) AS "Grupos mayoritarios distintos"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts.parquet') t
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/tracts-geom.parquet') g USING (geoid)
WHERE g.maxx > ${west:raw} AND g.minx < ${east:raw} AND g.maxy > ${south:raw} AND g.miny < ${north:raw}

spec.title: Ancestry Mosaic — the U.S. by census tract (ACS 2024)

spec.__legacyStringValue: SELECT ancestry FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/ancestry/ancestries.parquet') ORDER BY national_total DESC
